label: Rennet curd
comment: Set by rennet: the enzyme from a calf's stomach, or a microbial one.

about.text: Milk set into a soft gel by rennet, an extract of calves' stomachs whose working enzyme is chymosin, or by a substitute enzyme: it turns casein into paracasein, which links into a network that traps the fat. Cut, stirred, heated, drained and pressed to different degrees, it becomes most cheeses.

About 26 Mt of natural cheese (23.8 Mt of it from cows’ milk in 2023) from about 222 Mt of milk, at about 9 kg of milk a kilo: the curd weighs about what the cheese does.

how.text: Rennet makes the casein clot into a gel. Cutting the gel into grains lets the whey run out, and this whey is the sweet whey; cheese curd and sweet whey come from the one draining. The finer the cut, the drier the finished cheese.
